question: A train moves from City A to City B, a distance of 180 Kilometres in 3 hours. If the train keeps running at the same constant rate, how many hours will it take to travel the distance between City C and City D, which are 720 Kilometres apart?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Distance becomes 4 times: 720/180 = 4

⇒ Time will also become 4 times

⇒ Required time = 3 × 4 = 12 hours

**∴ Answer = 12 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance A→B = 180 km, Time = 3 hours

Distance C→D = 720 km

**Formula:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed = 180 / 3 = 60 km/hr

⇒ Time = 720 / 60 = 12 hours

**Final Answer: 12 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Speed Formula:** Speed = Distance / Time

**2. Direct Proportion:** At constant speed, time ∝ distance

**3. Unit Consistency:** Always keep km and hours consistent

**4. Scaling Trick:** If distance multiplies by n, time also multiplies by n
